title: Integrating Electrochemical Degradation Mechanisms into Fuzzy Fault Tree Analysis for Lithium-Ion Battery Systems Safety Assessment
content: Ensuring safety of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) requires accounting for complex degradation mechanisms and uncertain failure conditions that can lead to thermal runaway. This study developed an integrated risk assessment methodology combining Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) with fuzzy logic to identify the main failure pathways and to estimate the likelihood of thermal runaway initiation conditions for a generic Li-ion battery system. The fault tree incorporated abuse conditions (mechanical, electrical, thermal) and cooling system faults, including accelerating mechanisms such as ageing and other stress conditions, which are often neglected in other studies. Expert judgments were translated into fuzzy sets, aggregated using the Similarity Aggregation Method, and converted into probabilistic values for top-event evaluation. The importance analysis identified BTMS failure, cycling ageing, cooling-system fouling, and high ambient temperature as the most influential modeled basic events. Comparison with previously published studies confirmed consistency in the magnitude and relevance of key failure events. The methodology provided a robust and general framework for LIB safety assessment under uncertainty data conditions, independently on specific cell chemistry or application and the framework is directly transferable to battery packs and battery management systems of electric vehicles, ships, and aircraft.
